correctness.rationale: The explicit four distinct eigenvalues and spectral endpoint coefficients reconstruct the four-exponential kernel. The cubic-interpolation divided-difference identity and the third-derivative sign of s^alpha classify initial signs for every alpha>1, while stable subordination covers alpha<=1. A direct strict negative witness at time 1/2^alpha for alpha>=2, together with a three-zero Chebyshev bound and the positive late-time limit, gives exactly the asserted 0/1/2 positive crossings, with simplicity. Taylor expansions at alpha=1 and alpha=2 yield both onset constants; symbolic matrix and high-precision checks independently test finite instances but are not used to justify general quantifiers. No unverified infinite computation is invoked.

value.rationale: The four-path is a minimal non-complete-multipartite path example whose endpoint distance-three transfer sharply senses higher-order loss of positivity. The result is a complete real-power/positive-time sign classification, including a qualitatively new positive-negative-positive window and different square-root and linear bifurcation scales. It complements eventual-positivity theory by giving sharp recovery structure and could guide higher-order graph-diffusion interpretation. No unsupported whole-matrix positivity, general-graph, or global norm claim is inferred.
